ir.name: ref_all_pairs_builder
ir.intuition: Reference builder: all winner/loser pairs by objective ordering.

ir.name: pairwise_contrastive_advantage_reciprocal_clamped
ir.intuition: The original loss is identical to an existing one, so to reduce similarity and improve robustness, I added clamping of the inverse advantage gap to avoid excessively large values from very small gaps. This prevents instability from extremely high weights and adds a small epsilon margin to maintain numerical stability. This fixes novelty failure and ensures stable gradient updates while still emphasizing difficult pairs with small advantage gaps.
ir.pseudocode:
adv_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
log_prob_diff = batch['log_prob_w'] - batch['log_prob_l']
epsilon = 1e-6
inv_adv_raw = 1 / (abs(adv_gap) + epsilon)
inv_adv = clamp(inv_adv_raw, max=100.0)
score = log_prob_diff * inv_adv
loss = mean(weight * softplus(-score))
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch['weight']
    adv_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
    epsilon = 1e-6
    abs_adv = ops.add(ops.abs(adv_gap), epsilon)
    inv_adv_raw = ops.div(ops.ones_like(abs_adv), abs_adv)
    max_val = ops.ones_like(inv_adv_raw)
    max_val = ops.mul(max_val, 100.0)
    # Clamp inverse advantage to max 100 to prevent extreme values
    inv_adv = ops.minimum(inv_adv_raw, max_val)
    l_diff = ops.sub(lpw, lpl)
    score = ops.mul(l_diff, inv_adv)
    neg_score = ops.neg(score)
    loss_vec = ops.softplus(neg_score)
    loss_vec = ops.mul(loss_vec, weight)
    return ops.mean(loss_vec)
